name: Kushner Companies

summary.text: Kushner Companies is a New York real-estate firm controlled by the Kushner family; Jared Kushner was its chief executive until January 2017. In early 2007 the firm bought the office tower at 666 Fifth Avenue for about $1.8 billion, then the highest price paid for a single U.S. office building, mostly with debt; Vornado Realty Trust took a 49.5% interest in a 2011 restructuring. In 2016-17 the firm sought new investors for the building, including Anbang Insurance Group (talks ended March 2017) and Qatar's former prime minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim al-Thani, and met Qatar's finance minister in April 2017. On August 3, 2018 Brookfield Asset Management announced a 99-year, 100% leasehold interest in the office condominium acquired from Kushner Companies; terms were not disclosed. The Qatar Investment Authority held a 9% stake in Brookfield Property Partners; Brookfield and QIA both said Qatar had no involvement.

facts.claim: In early 2007 Kushner Companies bought the 41-storey office tower at 666 Fifth Avenue in Manhattan for about $1.8 billion, then the highest price ever paid for a single office building in the United States, in a deal financed mostly with debt.
facts.quote: Kushner's firm paid about $1.8 billion in early 2007, a price that was then the highest ever paid for a single U.S. office building.

sources.title: Kushner Companies offloads troubled 666 Fifth Avenue flagship
Kushner Reworks Debt on NYC's 666 Fifth Ave. With Vornado

facts.claim: In December 2011 Kushner Companies restructured the building's debt with Vornado Realty Trust, which paid $80 million and assumed half of the property's $1.2 billion mortgage for a 49.5% interest in the office portion; Kushner contributed $30 million. In 2018 Kushner Companies agreed to buy Vornado's 49.5% stake for $120 million, with Vornado saying the existing mortgage would be repaid.
facts.quote: Vornado paid $80 million and the assumption of half the property's $1.2 billion mortgage in 2011 for a 49.5% interest. Kushner contributed $30 million in that restructuring.

facts.claim: On March 29, 2017, Kushner Companies said it and China's Anbang Insurance Group had ended talks over an investment in 666 Fifth Avenue; a company spokesman said the firms had mutually agreed to end the talks and that the company remained in 'active, advanced negotiations' with other potential investors. Earlier reports had described Anbang providing as much as half of $2.5 billion in equity for a planned redevelopment; Anbang had said in a statement that 'there is no investment from Anbang for this deal.'
facts.quote: A Kushner spokesman said the firms had mutually agreed to end talks regarding the property. ... 'The information about Anbang investment in 666 Fifth Avenue is not correct, there is no investment from Anbang for this deal,' the company said in a statement.

facts.claim: The Intercept reported on July 10, 2017 that Jared Kushner and his father Charles Kushner negotiated throughout 2015 and 2016 with Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim al-Thani, Qatar's former prime minister, for an investment of about $500 million in 666 Fifth Avenue; according to the report, his commitment was contingent on Kushner Companies raising additional financing from other sources, which it did not, and the deal fell apart after Anbang withdrew.
facts.quote: Sources said HBJ's commitment was conditional: the deal was contingent on Kushner landing additional financing from other sources, which it failed to do, so it fell apart.

sources.title: Jared Kushner Tried and Failed to Get a Half-Billion-Dollar Bailout From Qatar

facts.claim: Charles Kushner confirmed that Kushner Companies met Qatar's finance minister in April 2017 at the St. Regis hotel in Manhattan, a meeting first reported by The Intercept. He said that before the meeting the company had decided not to accept sovereign wealth fund investment: 'We informed the Qatar representatives of our decision and they agreed.'
facts.quote: We informed the Qatar representatives of our decision and they agreed.

facts.claim: In May 2017 Nicole Kushner Meyer, Jared Kushner's sister and a Kushner Companies principal, promoted the firm's One Journal Square project in Jersey City to prospective EB-5 investors at events in Beijing (Ritz-Carlton) and Shanghai (Four Seasons); the offering sought 300 investors contributing a total of $150 million. She referred to her brother's White House role. Kushner Companies apologized 'if mention of her brother was in any way interpreted as an attempt to lure investors,' and spokesperson Risa Heller said executives would not attend the following weekend's events in China.
facts.quote: A spokesperson's statement apologized on her behalf if 'mention of her brother was in any way interpreted as an attempt to lure investors.' ... 'No one from Kushner Companies will be in China this weekend,' spokesperson Risa Heller said in a statement to the New York Times.

facts.claim: In August 2017 federal prosecutors in Brooklyn subpoenaed Kushner Companies over its use of the EB-5 investor-visa program, relating at least in part to One Journal Square. The company's general counsel said it 'utilized the program, fully complied with its rules and regulations and did nothing improper.'
facts.quote: The company's general counsel said it 'utilized the program, fully complied with its rules and regulations and did nothing improper.'

facts.claim: In May 2018, while Brookfield and Kushner Companies were reported to be near a deal, a Brookfield spokeswoman said: 'No Qatar-linked entity has any involvement in, investment in or even knowledge of this potential transaction.'
facts.quote: No Qatar-linked entity has any involvement in, investment in or even knowledge of this potential transaction.

facts.claim: On August 3, 2018, Brookfield Asset Management announced that it had acquired a 100% leasehold interest in the roughly 1.5 million-square-foot office condominium at 666 Fifth Avenue from Kushner Companies, for a term of 99 years, through one of its real-estate funds, with a major redevelopment planned. The release stated: 'Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.' Press reports put the upfront payment at about $1.1-1.3 billion.
facts.quote: The term of Brookfield's 100% leasehold interest in the office condominium, acquired from the Kushner Companies, will be 99 years. ... Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed.

facts.claim: Reporting on the Brookfield lease said the rent for the full 99-year term was paid upfront, and that the proceeds allowed Kushner Companies to pay down the building's roughly $1.1 billion debt and buy out Vornado. At the time of the announcement Kushner Companies declined to comment.
facts.quote: The debt-laden skyscraper was bailed out by Brookfield last August, when it took a 99-year lease on the property, paying the rent for 99 years upfront.

facts.claim: The Qatar Investment Authority bought a 9% stake in Brookfield Property Partners (BPY), the Brookfield real-estate unit, for $1.8 billion in 2014; the investment gave it no board seat. Reuters reported in February 2019, citing two sources, that the 666 Fifth Avenue transaction had prompted Qatar to decide that QIA would avoid funds or vehicles it did not control. A QIA spokesman told Reuters: 'QIA had absolutely no involvement in the 666 Fifth Avenue development and the claims about QIA's investment strategy are not true.'
facts.quote: QIA had absolutely no involvement in the 666 Fifth Avenue development and the claims about QIA's investment strategy are not true.

facts.claim: On December 9, 2020, Senator Ron Wyden and Representative Joaquin Castro opened an inquiry into the 666 Fifth Avenue transaction, writing to Brookfield; in October 2022 the Senate Finance Committee said documents showed Charles Kushner had engaged in discussions with Brookfield about the property on February 14, 2018, earlier than previously known, that QIA had invested $1.8 billion in BPY and was its second-largest investor, and that Brookfield had twice declined to provide the committee the information it requested.
facts.quote: New documents obtained by the Committees show that Charles Kushner, Mr. Kushner's father, engaged in discussions to bail out the property with Brookfield on February 14, 2018, which is earlier than previously known.

QIA held a 9% stake in Brookfield Property Partners, bought for $1.8 billion in 2014, when Brookfield took the 666 Fifth Avenue lease in 2018; QIA said it 'had absolutely no involvement' in the transaction and Brookfield said no Qatar-linked entity was involved. openQuestions: The Brookfield lease price was never disclosed; reports give $1.1 billion (Reuters/Bisnow 2019), $1.2 billion (Senate Finance Committee 2022) and $1.3 billion (Bisnow). No Kushner Companies statement on the August 2018 deal was found; the company declined to comment at the time. No Kushner Companies statement specifically denying QIA involvement was found; the denials recorded are Brookfield's (May 2018) and QIA's (February 2019).

QIA's rank among BPY investors is given as 'largest' by Crain's/Bloomberg (2018) and 'second-largest' by the Senate Finance Committee and Bisnow; the file records the committee's description with that attribution.

The Reuters February 2019 report on Qatar's investment-strategy review was reached only through Bisnow and Haaretz syndication; Reuters itself is unreachable. A later Reuters report that the Qatari government said it was involved through BPY (cited in the Senate committee's October 2022 letter) was not opened.

The Intercept's HBJ account rests on unnamed sources; the task's phrase 'Qatar's reported refusal' is not how the sources describe it: The Intercept describes a conditional commitment that lapsed, and Charles Kushner says the company declined sovereign wealth money. The April 2017 meeting is described as with Qatar's finance minister; the minister is not named in the sources reached.
Whether the One Journal Square EB-5 subpoena led to any action, and the outcome of Senator Grassley's requested review of the marketing claims, were not found.

The site has no entity id for Kushner Companies, Jared Kushner, Brookfield, Vornado or Anbang; this file uses the slug 'kushner-companies' and needs seeding. Bloomberg's 2011 article URL appeared in search results but its text was returned only in summary.
